Looking at the folded paper, the cut consists of a half‑circle notch on the fold edge plus a zigzag (star point) extending inward from that notch.

When unfolded, the half‑circle notch on the fold line becomes a full circle centered on the fold, and the zigzag point is mirrored to the other side, giving a circle with star points on both left and right, symmetric about the fold line.

- Option A has two separate circles with points facing inward — wrong (the cut touches the fold).
- Option B has circles at the center and stars at the outer edges — wrong placement.
- Option C is not symmetric about the fold line — impossible for an unfold.
- Option E has extra star cuts at the outer edges — not present in the folded cut.
- Option D shows exactly one circle centered on the fold with zigzag points on both sides — matching the mirror image of the cut.

\boxed{D}
